statement: The scores of a class on a test have a mean of $70$ points and a standard deviation of $8$ points. The teacher rescales every score using the rule $$\text{new score} = 1.2 \times (\text{old score}) + 5.$$ What are the mean and the standard deviation of the new scores?

choices.misconception: I applied the whole rule to the standard deviation, multiplying by 1.2 and then adding 5, but adding the same amount to every score does not change the spread.
I added the 5 points before multiplying by 1.2, so I got $1.2 \times 75 = 90$ for the mean, but the rule multiplies first.
I thought the standard deviation never changes when every score is changed by the same rule, but multiplying every score by 1.2 stretches the spread.

hints: Think about the two steps separately: multiplying every score, then adding to every score.
Both steps change the mean. Ask which step changes how spread out the scores are.
Multiplying by $1.2$ multiplies the mean and the standard deviation by $1.2$. Adding $5$ shifts the mean by $5$ but leaves the standard deviation alone.

solutions.reliable: Multiplying every score by $1.2$ gives a mean of $1.2(70) = 84$ and a standard deviation of $1.2(8) = 9.6$. Adding $5$ to every score shifts the mean to $89$ and does not change the distances between scores, so the standard deviation stays $9.6$. Check with two scores $62$ and $78$, one standard deviation below and above the mean: they become $79.4$ and $98.6$, which are $9.6$ below and above $89$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
